name: Fairbrooke Heights (scattered site)
headline: CARE Communities won 2026 federal 4% credits to renovate Fairbrooke Heights, its existing 36-unit, 2002-built tax credit apartment community in west Fort Collins, keeping all 36 homes affordable at 30-50% AMI.
why_it_matters: It is a small, deeply affordable preservation deal (average about 43% AMI) that a local nonprofit put together from bonds, 4% credits and a city gap grant shared with its Greenbriar property. That makes it a model for recapitalizing aging 1990s-2000s nonprofit tax credit stock in Larimer County.

status.label: Credits awarded; renovation planned to start around July 2027
status.detail: CHFA lists the award (amounts 'subject to change'). CARE told residents on 24 Sept 2026 that construction will begin around July 2027 and last about a year. No public record of a bond or financing closing or a building permit yet.

next_step: Watch for the Housing Catalyst bond issue and the financing closing (expected before the planned mid-2027 start), and for the City funding agreement that carries the $1.5M Greenbriar-Fairbrooke award.

background.text: CARE Housing (now CARE Communities) built Fairbrooke Heights as new construction with a 2001 CHFA 9% award: 36 units, 3 buildings, 100% low-income, nonprofit set-aside, 40-year extended use commitment. It was completed in 2002.

Because it is an acquisition/rehab deal, the property will move into a new tax credit ownership entity (inferred from the building type). CARE has done this before: in 2022 it rehabbed Swallow Road Apartments with Housing Catalyst as special limited partner and co-developer. No sale price or buyer entity for Fairbrooke is public.

Planned interior scope: energy-efficient lighting, heating and air conditioning, new kitchen and bath cabinets, appliances, water fixtures, washer and dryer, flooring and paint, water heaters, windows and blinds. Exterior: siding replacement, exterior stair repair, better outdoor community spaces and landscaping, ADA accessibility improvements, and trash and recycling enclosures.

Phasing: 6 phases of 6 units (half a building at a time), 6-8 weeks per phase. Residents either move permanently into a renovated unit or temporarily into another unit and return. CARE pays approved moving costs and will hire a relocation consultant; residents get 90-day and 30-day notices.

City gap funding: CARE asked for $1,500,000 for the combined Greenbriar-Fairbrooke Heights rehab (76 units, 0-60% AMI). The Affordable Housing Board ranked it last of 7 on 9 April 2026 ('not ready to proceed', 'no health & safety issues'). The Human Services and Housing Funding Board ranked it #3 and recommended full funding on 29 April 2026, and Council approved this in Resolution 2026-078 on the 16 June 2026 consent calendar.

Bond cap context: Council's 2026 city PAB allocation went to Country Ranch Apartments and Bristlecone Affordable (Resolution 2026-077), not to this deal. In 2025 the City assigned its full $11,184,752 cap to Housing Catalyst for CARE's Windtrail Park rehab 'and elsewhere in the City' (Resolution 2025-066). Housing Catalyst can carry cap forward for up to 3 years.

Before the rehab, a January 2024 market-study inventory listed Fairbrooke Heights with 35 LIHTC units (21 at 40% AMI and 14 at 50%) and rents set below the maximums. The new CHFA mix (3/18/15 at 30/40/50% AMI) is slightly deeper.
2026 CHFA maximum gross rents for Larimer County two-bedrooms: $880 at 30% AMI, $1,174 at 40% and $1,467 at 50%. Actual post-rehab rents are not public.
No Fairbrooke or CARE application appears on CHFA's Application Narratives Archive page, so there is no sign of a competitive 9% round attempt for this rehab.

discrepancies.text: Start date: CARE's English FAQ (dated 24 Sept 2026) says renovations begin 'in the first half of 2027' and take about 10 months. Its Spanish Fairbrooke section and the same-day resident presentation say 'around July 2027', running to June 2028 (about a year).
Bedrooms: CHFA shows 1 one-bedroom and 35 two-bedrooms, but CARE's community page describes Fairbrooke as '2-bedroom apartments'. The January 2024 market study does list a 1BR at Fairbrooke.

Existing income mix: the January 2024 market study's inventory table shows 21 units at 40% AMI and 14 at 50% (35 units), while its rent survey for 'Care at Fairbrooke Heights' also lists 30% AMI units. CHFA's new mix has 36 units including 3 at 30%.

open_questions: Whose bond cap backs the $3.4M of bonds (Housing Catalyst carryforward of the City's 2025 assignment, other local cap, or CHFA/statewide balance)? Not stated publicly.
Total development cost, acquisition price paid by the new partnership, tax credit investor and price, lender, general contractor and architect.

How the $1.5M city award is split between Fairbrooke and Greenbriar, and whether it is CDBG, HOME or Affordable Housing Fund money (federal money would bring Build America Buy America and Davis-Bacon-type requirements).
Length of the new affordability covenant (CARE said in 2025 that its Windtrail rehab would reset restrictions 'for at least another 60 years'; nothing equivalent is published for Fairbrooke).
Whether project-based vouchers will be added (CHFA shows no Section 8 contract).
